headline: Clinton took office in January, a van bomb hit the World Trade Center, and Waco ended in fire in April
texture: The Latur earthquake killed 9,748 people in Maharashtra on September 30. Bombs across Bombay killed 257 on March 12, two months after riots in the same city. The Storm of the Century crossed the eastern United States from March 13 to 15 with record snowfall and reportedly killed 184 people between Cuba and Quebec. The Mississippi and Missouri flooded the Midwest from April to October and peaked on August 1. A bridge gave way under the Amtrak Sunset Limited at Big Bayou Canot on September 22, killing 47. Every member of the Zambian national football team died in a crash off Libreville on April 27.

Depeche Mode took questions from fans on AOL on September 20, and the band and much of the audience could not get logged in. Adobe published the first version of the PDF format on June 15, alongside Acrobat 1.0. Microsoft shipped Windows NT 3.1 on July 27 and Windows 3.11 for Workgroups in November. Nintendo and Silicon Graphics began work on Project Reality on October 1. Congress opened hearings on violence in video games on December 7, more than six months after Sega of America set up the first content rating council for the industry.

Ross Perot and Al Gore argued about NAFTA on Larry King's CNN programme on November 9, in front of 11.174 million households, the largest audience an advertising-supported cable network had drawn. ESPN2 signed on October 1 and TV Food Network on November 22, where Emeril Lagasse hosted How to Boil Water. The first Got Milk? advertisement ran on October 29, built around a man who knows who shot Alexander Hamilton and cannot say it clearly with his mouth full of peanut butter. The Ultimate Fighting Championship sold its first pay-per-view from Denver on November 12.

Prince announced on his 35th birthday, June 7, that he was changing his name to an unpronounceable symbol. Kim Campbell became Canada's first female prime minister on June 25, lost the October 25 election that cut the Progressive Conservatives to two seats, and gave up the party leadership on December 13. South Africa abandoned its nuclear weapons programme in March, and on December 7 the Transitional Executive Committee met in Cape Town, the first official government body in the country with Black members.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: First year in office, from January 20. George H. W. Bush held the office until that morning, and Dan Quayle was Vice President until then, with Al Gore taking over. William Rehnquist was Chief Justice, Tom Foley Speaker of the House and George J. Mitchell Senate majority leader. The 102nd Congress sat until January 3 and the 103rd afterwards, and Clinton gave his first address to it on February 17. Janet Reno was confirmed as Attorney General on March 11 and sworn in the next day, and Ruth Bader Ginsburg was sworn in as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court on August 10.

pol.inauguration.label: Clinton inaugurated
pol.inauguration.value: Sworn in as the 42nd president of the United States, with Al Gore sworn in as the 45th vice president
pol.inauguration.detail: The Constitution starts a presidential term on January 20, and both cached year pages give that day. Neither carries anything beyond the two oaths, so this fact cites the dedicated article, pulled as raw wikitext and the only source in this file from outside the cache. It gives Wednesday, January 20 at the West Front of the United States Capitol, calls it the 52nd inauguration, and names Chief Justice William Rehnquist as administering the presidential oath at noon and Associate Justice Byron White the vice presidential oath. Maya Angelou read her poem On the Pulse of Morning after the address, the second poet to read at an inauguration after Robert Frost.

pol.wtc_bombing.label: World Trade Center bombing
pol.wtc_bombing.value: A van bomb parked below the North Tower exploded, killing six people and injuring more than a thousand
pol.wtc_bombing.detail: Both cached year pages carry the same casualty figures and neither gives a cost. Authorities announced the capture of a suspected conspirator, Mohammad Salameh, on March 4.

pol.waco.label: Waco siege ends
pol.waco.value: A fire ended the 51-day stand-off at the Branch Davidian compound near Waco, Texas, killing 76 people including David Koresh
pol.waco.detail: Agents of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms had raided the compound on February 28 with a warrant for Koresh on federal firearms violations. Four agents and five Davidians died that day and the stand-off began. The television page says NBC broadcast a hastily produced television movie about the siege on May 23, with Tim Daly as Koresh.

pol.nafta.label: NAFTA signed
pol.nafta.value: Clinton signed the North American Free Trade Agreement into law
pol.nafta.detail: The agreement had passed the legislative houses of the United States, Canada and Mexico between November 17 and 22.

pol.brady.label: Brady Act signed
pol.brady.value: Clinton signed the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act, which requires buyers of handguns to pass a background check

world.new_states.label: New states on the map
value: Czechoslovakia ceased to exist on January 1, as the Czech Republic and Slovakia separated
Macedonia was admitted to the United Nations on April 8 under the provisional reference the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia
Eritreans voted overwhelmingly for independence from Ethiopia on April 23 in a referendum monitored by the United Nations
Eritrea became independent on May 24 and entered the United Nations with Monaco on May 28
world.new_states.detail: Vaclav Havel was elected President of the Czech Republic on January 26, and the science page says both new countries joined CERN. The year page dates the United Nations verification of the Eritrean vote to April 27.

world.european_union.label: Maastricht Treaty takes effect
world.european_union.value: The treaty entered into force and formally established the European Union
world.european_union.detail: The European Economic Community had eliminated trade barriers and created a single market on January 1. In August the European Exchange Rate Mechanism margin was widened to 15 percent to absorb speculation against the French franc and other currencies.

world.oslo_accord.label: Oslo I Accord
world.oslo_accord.value: Yasser Arafat and Yitzhak Rabin shook hands in Washington after signing a peace accord, following talks held in secret earlier in the year
world.oslo_accord.detail: The year page carries the handshake and the secret talks in one line and names no mediator.

world.mogadishu.label: Battle of Mogadishu
world.mogadishu.value: Task Force Ranger fought Somali militia after two Black Hawk helicopters were shot down, leaving 18 Americans dead, one captured and more than 74 wounded, and over 1,000 Somalis dead
world.mogadishu.detail: The operation was called Gothic Serpent. The year page dates the fighting to October 3 and 4 and the US year page carries October 3 alone. UNOSOM II had taken over the United Nations duties in Somalia from UNITAF on May 4, and twenty-four Pakistani troops in the United Nations force were killed in Mogadishu on June 5.

world.russia.label: Tanks clear the Russian parliament
world.russia.value: Military and security forces took the White House of Russia by force, quashing a mass uprising against President Boris Yeltsin
world.russia.detail: A referendum on April 25, during the power struggle between president and parliament, expressed confidence in Yeltsin and his reforms while rejecting early elections.

world.bosnia.label: Bosnian War
value: Srebrenica was declared a protected safe area by the United Nations on April 16
Members of the Jokeri unit of the Croatian Defence Council entered Ahmici the same day and killed 120 Muslim residents
The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia was created in The Hague on May 25
Bosnian Croat forces destroyed the Stari Most, the old bridge at Mostar, by tank fire on November 9
world.bosnia.detail: Security Council Resolution 808 of February 22 had decided that an international tribunal should be established, and Resolution 827 created it. Large protests against Slobodan Milosevic's government filled Belgrade on June 1, and the opposition leader Vuk Draskovic and his wife Danica were arrested.

world.escobar.label: Pablo Escobar killed
world.escobar.value: Colombian police gunned down the drug trafficker
world.escobar.detail: The year page carries the killing in one line and gives no location.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, worldwide
value: Jurassic Park, $914,691,118, Universal
Mrs. Doubtfire, $441,286,195, 20th Century Fox
The Fugitive, $368,875,760, Warner Bros.
Schindler's List, $321,306,305, Universal
The Firm, $270,248,367, Paramount
film.gross.detail: Worldwide box-office gross rather than domestic rentals. The table's column header reads Rank, Title, Distributor, Worldwide gross, and the sentence directly above it calls the entries the top ten films released this year by worldwide gross, so header and text agree. A hidden comment inside the Jurassic Park cell warns editors not to substitute the lifetime gross, because the figure given covers the initial theatrical run. Indecent Proposal was sixth at $266,614,059 for Paramount, Cliffhanger seventh at $255,000,211, Sleepless in Seattle eighth at $227,799,884 and Philadelphia ninth at $206,678,440, all three for TriStar, and The Pelican Brief tenth at $195,268,056 for Warner Bros.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.value: Schindler's List, produced by Steven Spielberg, Gerald R. Molen and Branko Lustig
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded the following spring at the 66th Academy Awards, held at the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion in Los Angeles and hosted by Whoopi Goldberg, who the ceremony page says was the first African American and the first woman to host the telecast solo. Billy Crystal had declined after four consecutive ceremonies, and Gil Cates offered the job to Steve Martin, Bette Midler and Johnny Carson before Goldberg took it. Schindler's List won seven awards from twelve nominations, the most of either kind, and Spielberg took Best Director. The other Best Picture nominees were The Fugitive, In the Name of the Father, The Piano and The Remains of the Day. Jurassic Park and The Piano won three awards each. The telecast on ABC ran three hours and 18 minutes and drew 46.26 million viewers for a 31.86 Nielsen share.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting Oscars
value: Best Actor, Tom Hanks, Philadelphia
Best Actress, Holly Hunter, The Piano
Best Supporting Actor, Tommy Lee Jones, The Fugitive
Best Supporting Actress, Anna Paquin, The Piano
film.acting_awards.detail: Jane Campion won original screenplay for The Piano and Steven Zaillian adapted screenplay for Schindler's List, from the book by Thomas Keneally. John Williams won original score and Bruce Springsteen original song for Streets of Philadelphia, and Janusz Kaminski cinematography. Holly Hunter was nominated twice, as lead for The Piano and supporting for The Firm, and Emma Thompson twice, as lead for The Remains of the Day and supporting for In the Name of the Father. Leonardo DiCaprio was nominated for What's Eating Gilbert Grape and Ralph Fiennes for Schindler's List, and Angela Bassett and Laurence Fishburne both for What's Love Got to Do with It. The film page's awards table gives the Golden Globe for drama to Schindler's List and for comedy or musical to Mrs. Doubtfire, with Robin Williams best actor there, and the BAFTA award for best film to Schindler's List with Anthony Hopkins best actor for The Remains of the Day.

film.world_cinema.label: Nominated for Best Foreign Language Film
value: Belle Epoque, Spain, in Spanish, directed by Fernando Trueba, the winner
Farewell My Concubine, Hong Kong, in Mandarin, directed by Chen Kaige
Hedd Wyn, United Kingdom, in Welsh, directed by Paul Turner
The Scent of Green Papaya, Vietnam, in Vietnamese, directed by Anh Hung Tran
The Wedding Banquet, Taiwan, in Mandarin, directed by Ang Lee
film.world_cinema.detail: The ceremony page states each film's country, language and director. Farewell My Concubine took both the Golden Globe and the BAFTA award in the same category, by the film page's awards table. On January 1 the China Film Import and Export Corporation lost its 40-year monopoly on distributing every film in China, and 16 other Chinese studios became responsible for distributing their own. None of the cached pages carries the Cannes, Venice or Berlin prizes for the year, so no festival winner is named here.

film.releases.label: Releases and studio changes
value: Jurassic Park, June 11, Universal, with a record $50 million opening weekend
Indecent Proposal, April 7, Paramount, which the film page calls controversial
Super Mario Bros., May 28, Hollywood Pictures, the first film made from a video game, with Bob Hoskins as Mario and John Leguizamo as Luigi
Last Action Hero, June 18, which the film page calls a commercial disappointment for Arnold Schwarzenegger
Schindler's List, December 15, Universal
film.releases.detail: The film page dates Jurassic Park to June 11 and so do both cached year pages, while the science page gives June 9. It set opening records in Mexico and the United Kingdom on July 16 and in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan the next day, and the film page calls it the highest-grossing film ever made at a worldwide gross above $900 million. Super Mario Bros. took only $20.9 million in the domestic market. Bram Stoker's Dracula opened in the United Kingdom on January 29 with a record opening weekend the film page gives as 2,633,635 pounds, printed with a stray word million after the figure. Brandon Lee was killed on March 31 during the filming of The Crow, and River Phoenix died on October 31 during the filming of Dark Blood. Kim Basinger filed for bankruptcy on May 27 after a California judge ordered her to pay $8.9 million for refusing to honour a verbal contract to star in Boxing Helena, and lost the town of Braselton, Georgia to her partner in that purchase, the pension fund of Ameritech. Turner Broadcasting System acquired Castle Rock Entertainment on December 22.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, and at home when a network scheduled a film. Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade had its network premiere on CBS on March 2 and Home Alone on NBC on November 25.
film.how_people_watched.detail: Fox showed The Rocky Horror Picture Show on October 25 with the film intercut with a live cast performing along to it. None of the cached pages says anything about tape rental, laser disc or the price of either, so this fact claims nothing about them. The average ticket price was $4.14.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 1993
value: 60 Minutes, CBS, 20.9 rating
Home Improvement, ABC, 20.4
Seinfeld, NBC, 19.4
Roseanne, ABC, 19.1
Grace Under Fire, ABC, 17.7
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season, so this ranking covers the season that opened in the autumn and ran into the following spring. Coach was sixth on 17.4 for ABC, Frasier seventh on 16.8 for NBC, Monday Night Football eighth on 16.5 for ABC, Murphy Brown ninth on 16.3 for CBS and the CBS Sunday Movie tenth on 16.2. NYPD Blue tied for 18th on 13.9 with Wings.

tv.cheers_finale.label: Cheers ends
tv.cheers_finale.value: 80.4 million people watched the series finale on NBC, which followed an hour-long fourth-season finale of Seinfeld
tv.cheers_finale.detail: Cheers had started in 1982. The Seinfeld episode closed a season-long story about a pilot Jerry and George wrote, which NBC executives refuse at the end of it. Knots Landing ended on May 13 after starting in 1979, The Wonder Years on May 12, Quantum Leap on May 5 and A Different World on July 9.

tv.late_night.label: Letterman moves to CBS
tv.late_night.value: David Letterman broadcast his last Late Night for NBC on June 25 and premiered the Late Show on CBS on August 30, with Bill Murray and Billy Joel as his first guests
tv.late_night.detail: He had announced the move on January 14. Lorne Michaels picked Conan O'Brien, then a writer on The Simpsons, on April 25 to take the NBC slot after The Tonight Show, and Late Night with Conan O'Brien premiered on September 13. The Chevy Chase Show ended on October 1 after starting the same year.

tv.premieres.label: Programs that debuted
value: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, syndication, January 3
WWF Monday Night Raw, USA Network, January 11
Homicide: Life on the Street, NBC, January 31
Beavis and Butt-Head, MTV, March 8
Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, Fox Kids, August 28
The X-Files, Fox, September 10
Frasier, NBC, September 16
NYPD Blue, ABC, September 21
Boy Meets World, ABC, September 24
tv.premieres.detail: The television page's premiere table gives each date and network. The X-Files pilot took a 7.9 Nielsen rating, 7.4 million households and 12.0 million viewers. At least 30 ABC affiliates, mostly in smaller markets, refused to carry NYPD Blue over nudity and language uncommon on broadcast television at the time. Power Rangers used stock footage from the Japanese series Kyoryu Sentai Zyuranger. Britney Spears, Justin Timberlake, Christina Aguilera and Ryan Gosling joined the cast of The New Mickey Mouse Club on October 4, and Michael J. Nelson replaced Joel Hodgson as host of Mystery Science Theater 3000 on October 30.

tv.nfl_rights.label: Fox buys the NFL
tv.nfl_rights.value: CBS lost the rights to National Football Conference games to Fox, which offered a record $1.58 billion
tv.nfl_rights.detail: CBS had broadcast National Football League games for 38 years. Its Major League Baseball contract ended too, on October 23, after the owners approved a six-year joint venture with ABC and NBC on May 28 that displaced CBS as baseball's primary network.

music.hot100_year_end.label: Year-end Hot 100 singles
value: I Will Always Love You, Whitney Houston
Whoomp! (There It Is), Tag Team
Can't Help Falling in Love, UB40
That's the Way Love Goes, Janet Jackson
Freak Me, Silk
music.hot100_year_end.detail: From the year in music edition of Billboard dated December 25. I Will Always Love You posted its 14th week at number one on March 6, and That's the Way Love Goes spent eight consecutive weeks there from May. Whitney Houston had three songs on the chart and SWV three inside the top 40, with Weak at six, I'm So Into You at 20 and Right Here at 29. Janet Jackson charted three from her album, with If at 19 and Again at 74. Weak was sixth, If I Ever Fall in Love by Shai seventh, Dreamlover by Mariah Carey eighth, Rump Shaker by Wreckx-n-Effect ninth and Informer by Snow tenth.

music.listening_format.label: How people listened
music.listening_format.value: Sales were counted by computer. The Bodyguard: Original Soundtrack Album sold more than a million copies in one American week on January 9, which the music page calls the first album to do so since Nielsen SoundScan introduced computerised sales monitoring in May 1992.
music.listening_format.detail: Janet Jackson's fifth album sold 350,000 copies in its first week from May 18, the highest opening week by a woman to that point and the first album by a woman to debut at number one in the SoundScan era. MTV Latin America launched on October 1, and Nirvana played their unplugged concert for MTV in New York on November 18. No cached page compares compact discs with cassettes or names a radio format for the year, so this fact claims nothing about either.

music.best_selling_album.label: Best-selling albums of the year
value: The Bodyguard: Original Soundtrack Album, Whitney Houston
Breathless, Kenny G
Unplugged, Eric Clapton
janet., Janet Jackson
Some Gave All, Billy Ray Cyrus
music.best_selling_album.detail: The Chronic by Dr. Dre was sixth, Pocket Full of Kryptonite by the Spin Doctors seventh, Ten by Pearl Jam eighth, The Chase by Garth Brooks ninth and Core by Stone Temple Pilots tenth. The music page ranks the ten and gives no sales figure for any of them.

music.eurovision.label: Eurovision Song Contest
music.eurovision.value: Niamh Kavanagh won for Ireland with In Your Eyes, at the Green Glens Arena in Millstreet
music.eurovision.detail: The win brought Ireland level with France and Luxembourg on five victories, and Ireland was hosting. The 22nd OTI Festival, at the Teatro Principal in Valencia on October 9, was won by Enamorarse, written by Alejandro Abad and Josep Llobell and performed by Ana Reverte for Spain.

music.jackson_investigation.label: Michael Jackson investigated
music.jackson_investigation.value: News broke that he was under investigation over allegations of child molestation, and a civil suit followed on September 14 from a thirteen-year-old boy and his parents
music.jackson_investigation.detail: Jackson ended the Dangerous World Tour in Mexico City on November 11 and made his first public statement on December 22, in a videotaped address calling the accusations totally false and asking the public to wait to hear the truth. The music page names the boy who brought the suit and this fact does not.

tech.web_use.label: Mosaic released
tech.web_use.value: Version 1.0 of the Mosaic web browser, devised by Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina, was released in the United States
tech.web_use.detail: The science page carries the release and nothing else about it. No cached page counts internet users, names a web site or says what a connection cost this year, so this fact claims none of that.

tech.spam.label: The word spamming
tech.spam.value: A bug in a program written by Richard Depew sent one article to 200 newsgroups at once, and Joel Furr coined the term spamming for the incident

tech.pentium.label: First Pentium chips
tech.pentium.value: Intel began shipping them on March 22
tech.pentium.detail: The science page and the US year page carry the same date and neither gives a clock speed or a price.

tech.games.label: Video games
value: Star Fox, Nintendo, February 21, the first game to use the Super FX chip
The 7th Guest, Virgin Interactive, April 1, which sold over two million copies on MS-DOS
Myst, Cyan and Broderbund, September 24
Virtua Fighter, Sega, October, the first fully polygonal fighting game
Mortal Kombat II, Midway, November
Doom, id Software, December 10, on MS-DOS
NBA Jam, Midway, December, one of the first sports games with licensed teams and players
tech.games.detail: The games page calls Street Fighter II the highest-grossing entertainment product of the year, earning more than the film Jurassic Park, at $1.5 billion worldwide in coin drop, and puts NBA Jam above $300 million in American arcades. Panasonic, GoldStar and Sanyo released the first versions of the 3DO, Atari released the Jaguar and called it the first 64-bit video game system, Fujitsu released the FM Towns Marty in Japan as the first 32-bit home console and Commodore released the Amiga CD32. Sega released the Model 2 arcade board, which introduced texture filtering. The page names Samurai Shodown as game of the year in the Electronic Gaming Monthly vote, and Disney's Aladdin, released for the Genesis on November 11, as Genesis game of the year in the public vote at the Electronic Gaming Awards.

tech.hubble_repair.label: Hubble repaired in orbit
tech.hubble_repair.value: NASA launched STS-61 on Endeavour to install corrective optics for the telescope's flawed mirror, and the first corrected images were taken on December 20
tech.hubble_repair.detail: The science page says the upgrades took magnification and clarity past the original design, and that the telescope had been designed for servicing of this kind. Both cached year pages carry the December 2 launch.

tech.fermat.label: A proof of Fermat's Last Theorem announced
tech.fermat.value: Andrew Wiles presented it at the Isaac Newton Institute
tech.fermat.detail: The two cached pages disagree on the date. The science page gives June 21 at the Isaac Newton Institute and says the proof as announced was slightly flawed, while the year page dates his worldwide fame to June 24 and says nothing about a flaw. This fact takes the science page's date and names the disagreement rather than resolving it.

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Unleaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31. The chart gives April 1991 as the date it rose to this rate.

prices.unemployment.label: US unemployment rate
prices.unemployment.value: 6.5 percent in December, the lowest since January 1991
prices.unemployment.detail: The US year page carries the December figure and no annual average. IBM had announced a loss of $4,970,000,000 for the previous year on January 19, which the same page calls the largest single-year corporate loss in United States history to that date.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: Both of the year's American disasters played out on live television, a bombed tower in February and a burning compound in April. A browser was something you heard about from someone who already had one. Dinosaurs took the summer and a Whitney Houston ballad held the top of the singles chart into March.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Literature, Toni Morrison
Peace, Nelson Mandela and F. W. de Klerk
Physics, Russell Alan Hulse and Joseph Hooton Taylor Jr.
Chemistry, Kary Mullis and Michael Smith
Medicine, Richard J. Roberts and Phillip Allen Sharp
Economics, Robert W. Fogel and Douglass North
culture.nobel_prizes.detail: The year page lists the six and dates none of them. The science page carries the same names for physics, chemistry and medicine, and gives the Turing Award to Juris Hartmanis and Richard E. Stearns.

culture.dont_ask_dont_tell.label: Don't ask, don't tell announced
culture.dont_ask_dont_tell.value: Clinton announced the policy on homosexuals serving in the American military
culture.dont_ask_dont_tell.detail: An executive order of April 28 had already required the United States Air Force to allow women to fly in combat.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: Toronto Blue Jays beat the Philadelphia Phillies four games to two, and Joe Carter ended it with a walk-off home run
sports.world_series.detail: Paul Molitor was series most valuable player. The sports page calls Carter's the second walk-off home run ever to end a World Series and the first by an American League player, and the year page calls Toronto the first team to win back-to-back titles since the New York Yankees of 1977 and 1978. Lee Smith broke the all-time save record with his 358th on April 13 in a 9 to 7 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers, and Randy Myers saved 53 games for the Chicago Cubs, a record for left-handers.

sports.super_bowl.label: Super Bowl XXVII
sports.super_bowl.value: Dallas Cowboys beat the Buffalo Bills 52 to 17 at the Rose Bowl in front of 98,374, with the quarterback Troy Aikman named most valuable player
sports.super_bowl.detail: The US year page says the Bills became the first team to lose three consecutive Super Bowls. Michael Jackson played the halftime show, the first solo performer to do it, in a medley of his hits that the television page says was a ratings success. Alabama beat Miami 34 to 13 in the Sugar Bowl on January 1 for the college national championship of the previous season, and the NFL introduced its free agency system on March 1.

sports.champions.label: Other championships
value: Stanley Cup, Montreal Canadiens over the Los Angeles Kings, four games to one
NBA Finals, Chicago Bulls over the Phoenix Suns, four games to two, a third title in a row
NCAA basketball, North Carolina 77, Michigan 71
Grey Cup, Edmonton Eskimos 33, Winnipeg Blue Bombers 23
Premier League, Manchester United, the inaugural title and their first league championship in 26 years
UEFA Champions League, Olympique de Marseille 1, A.C. Milan 0
World Snooker Championship, Stephen Hendry over Jimmy White, 18 to 5
sports.champions.detail: The sports page carries Michael Jordan's retirement announcement of October 6 in the same entry as the Bulls' title, and names him Associated Press Male Athlete of the Year with Sheryl Swoopes the female winner. Julie Krone became the first woman to win a Triple Crown race, on Colonial Affair in the Belmont Stakes, Sea Hero won the Kentucky Derby and Prairie Bayou the Preakness, and the Grand National was declared void. Bernhard Langer took the Masters, Lee Janzen the US Open, Greg Norman the British Open and Paul Azinger the PGA Championship, with Nick Price leading the money list at $1,478,557, and the United States won the Ryder Cup 15 to 13. Mario Lemieux took both the Art Ross and the Hart trophies. France won the 99th Five Nations Championship. Australia beat England 4 to 0 in the Ashes, and Shane Warne bowled the ball of the century to Mike Gatting at Old Trafford on June 4.

sports.seles.label: Monica Seles stabbed
sports.seles.value: The top-ranked women's player was stabbed in the back during a changeover at the Citizen Cup in Hamburg, by a fan of her rival Steffi Graf
sports.seles.detail: Seles had won the Australian Open in January. Graf won the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open, Pete Sampras took Wimbledon and the US Open among the men, Jim Courier the Australian Open and Sergi Bruguera the French Open, and Germany won the Davis Cup 4 to 1 over Australia.

sports.expansion.label: New franchises
value: Colorado Rockies and Florida Marlins played their first Major League Baseball seasons, the first expansion in 16 seasons
The Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and the Florida Panthers played their first National Hockey League seasons
sports.expansion.detail: Both new baseball teams entered the National League. The US year page adds the Sacramento Gold Miners, established on February 23 as the first American franchise in the Canadian Football League, and the television page says Gayle Gardner became the first woman to call play-by-play on a televised baseball game, a Rockies game against the Cincinnati Reds on August 3.

sports.olympic_host.label: Sydney chosen as an Olympic host
sports.olympic_host.value: The International Olympic Committee selected Sydney, Australia, as the host city of a future Summer Olympics

deaths.hepburn.label: Audrey Hepburn
deaths.hepburn.detail: Actress, in Breakfast at Tiffany's and Roman Holiday.

deaths.marshall.label: Thurgood Marshall
deaths.marshall.detail: Jurist, the first African American on the Supreme Court.

deaths.ashe.label: Arthur Ashe
deaths.ashe.detail: Tennis player, of complications from HIV, which the US year page says he was believed to have contracted from a blood transfusion during heart surgery ten years earlier.

deaths.fellini.label: Federico Fellini
deaths.fellini.detail: Italian director and screenwriter, of 8 1/2 and Amarcord.

notes: Research pass July 2026, from the cached wikitext under .sources/1993. figures_basis is gross, checked with bo.mjs rather than assumed: the column header reads Rank, Title, Distributor, Worldwide gross, and the sentence directly above the table calls the entries the top ten films released this year by worldwide gross, so header and text agree and there is no rentals gloss to write. film.gross says worldwide in both its label and its detail, because the neighbouring years' tables are not all on the same basis and a reader comparing two years is otherwise comparing different measurements. A hidden comment inside the Jurassic Park cell tells editors not to replace the figure with the lifetime gross, so the fact repeats that warning rather than substituting a bigger number. Date checks. An inauguration falls this year and carries a checkable constitutional constraint, so pol.inauguration cites https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Bill_Clinton, pulled as raw wikitext and the only source in this file from outside the cache. It gives Wednesday, January 20 at the West Front of the Capitol, calls it the 52nd inauguration, and names William Rehnquist administering the presidential oath at noon and Byron White the vice presidential oath. Both cached year pages give January 20 and the two oaths and nothing else, so there is no disagreement to name, only a gap the dedicated article fills.
